title: NAFLD definition, NASH histology, risk factors and progression
guide: Macrovesicular fat ≥5% hepatocytes; 80% IFL vs 20% NASH; ballooning, steatosis degree, lobular inflammation, chicken-wire zone-3 fibrosis; established (obesity, T2DM/IR, dyslipidemia, MetS, PCOS, starvation, ↓adiponectin, leptin resistance), other (hypothyroid, OSA, hypopituitarism, hypogonadism, pancreatoduodenal resection, psoriasis), drugs (L-asparaginase, bleomycin, tetracycline, griseofulvin, valproate, amiodarone); 2-hit, 10–15% over 15 yrs, direct HCC only in NASH & HBV.

title: Clinical features, investigations, fibroscan and the ALT/AST algorithm
guide: Vague RUQ pain, fatigue, malaise; hepatomegaly; rare splenomegaly (PHTN), spider angiomata (liver failure), palmar erythema, ascites (decompensation); biopsy, ferritin, USG → MR elastography > transient elastography, ALT/AST; Vs 1.1/1.7/3.6 m/s ≈ 3/9/40 kPa, F0–F4; normal → IFL; <150 AST<ALT → NASH → fibroscan N/↑↑; AST>ALT → cirrhosis.

title: Treatment: lifestyle and drugs
guide: 10% weight loss over 6 months; 30–45 min × 5 days/week; omega-3, caffeine; vitamin E DOC 800–1000 U/day, improves NASH, unknown in cirrhosis, ~2 years; saroglitazar 4 mg dual PPAR-α/γ; pioglitazone PPAR-γ may be tried; oral semaglutide GLP-1 RA.
